candidate.blueprint_locator: 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan, Health Promotion and Maintenance, printed p.9 / PDF p.13
candidate.educational_objective: Explain the cavity-prevention role of appropriately used fluoride in children.

options.A: Fluoride helps rebuild and strengthen tooth enamel and reduces the risk of dental caries when used appropriately
options.B: Fluoride is used primarily to whiten teeth and does not affect cavity risk
options.C: Fluoride should be avoided in all children because it weakens developing enamel
options.D: Fluoride prevents every cavity, so brushing and other oral-hygiene measures are unnecessary

candidate.rationale: CDC states that fluoride repairs and prevents damage to teeth, replaces minerals lost from the tooth surface, makes enamel harder to dissolve, and helps prevent cavities. Pediatric use should be age-appropriate and used as directed.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Supports fluoride-mediated remineralization/enamel protection and prevention of cavities in children and adults.
candidate.source_locator: How does fluoride work?; Types of fluoride products
candidate.source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
candidate.stem: A parent asks why fluoride is included in a child's dental-health plan. Which response by the nurse is best?
